newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Airbus announces orders for up to 38 planes.
newsitem.headline: Airbus announces orders for up to 38 planes.

text.p: The European Airbus Industrie consortium announced in Singapore on Tuesday it had won orders for up to 38 aircraft, prompting a flap with one of the potential customers.

In three separate statements, Airbus said the 26 firm orders and 12 options were placed by three companies -- Hong Kong-based commercial carrier Cathay Pacific Airways, Germany's Condor Flugdienst charter airline and Federal Express, the U.S.-based cargo and courier service.

But Condor promptly denied the Airbus statement that it would buy 12 A320s for delivery in 1998 and 1999 with an option for 12 more. The planes would replace Condor's Boeing 737 fleet on European routes.
"We have not ordered any Airbuses," a Condor spokeswoman said in Frankfurt.
But then Airbus senior vice-president John Leahy said the consortium had initialled an order with Condor.
He told a news conference at the Fairnborough airshow near London that Airbus still had only a memorandum of understanding with Condor and was awaiting board approval from the airline.

Airbus said in the Singapore statement Condor would be buying for the first time from the consortium of France's Aerospatial, British Aerospace plc, Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace and Casa of Spain.
It said in a second statement Federal Express ordered 11 A300-600 freighter aircraft for delivery between 1998 and 2000.

Airbus said the planes would be powered by General Electric CF6-80C2 engines and used primarily on domestic routes in the United States. Federal Express previously ordered 25 A300-600Fs in 1991, it said.
It also said Cathay Pacific Airways had signed a contract for three more ultra long-range A340-300s, increasing to nine the number of firm orders placed by the airline for the four-engine aircraft.
Cathay's planes would be delivered during the second and third quarters of 1998 and would operate between Hong Kong and Europe and North America, it said.
